# Sirach Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_003_page_001.jpg

---

1 Listen to me, your father, O children; act accordingly, so that you may be safe.

2 For the Lord gave the father authority over his children, and established the right of the mother over her sons.

3 Whoever honors his father atones for sins,

4 and whoever glorifies his mother is like one who lays up treasure.

5 Whoever honors his father will be gladdened by his own children, and when he prays he will be heard.

6 Whoever glorifies his father will have long life, and whoever obeys the Lord brings comfort to his mother.

7 He who fears the Lord honors his father, and serves his parents as his masters.

8 Honor your father in word and deed, so that his blessing may come upon you.

9 For a father's blessing builds up the children's homes, but a mother's curse tears out their foundations.

10 Do not seek honor for yourself by dishonoring your father; for your father's dishonor brings no honor to you.

11 A man's honor comes from his father's glory, and a shameful mother is a reproach to her children.

12 My child, care for your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives.

13 Even if his understanding fails, show patience with him; do not despise him all the days of his life.

14 For kindness shown to a father will not be forgotten; it will stand as an offering against your sins.

15 In the day of your trouble it will be remembered in your favor; like frost in sunshine, your sins will melt.

16 Whoever abandons his father is like a blasphemer; and whoever provokes his mother is cursed by God.

17 My child, go about your work with humility, and you will be loved more than a generous giver.

18 The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; and you will find favor before the Lord.

19 Many are great and renowned, but to the humble he reveals his secrets.

20 For great is the power of the Lord, and he is glorified by the humble.

21 Do not seek what is too hard for you; do not investigate what is beyond your strength.

22 Meditate on what has been given to you; for you have no need of what is hidden.

23 Do not busy yourself with what is beyond your task; for more has been shown to you than you can grasp.

24 For many have been led astray by their own presumption, and false imagination has caused their thinking to slip.

25 Without eyes there is no light; without knowledge, no wisdom.

26 A stubborn heart will come to grief in the end; and one who loves danger will perish by it.

27 A stubborn heart will be burdened with trouble; the sinner piles up sin upon sin.

28 For the proud there is no cure for their affliction; a harmful plant has taken root in them.

29 An intelligent mind will reflect on a proverb; a discerning ear is what a wise person desires.

30 Water extinguishes a blazing fire; so almsgiving atones for sin.

31 Whoever repays a kindness is mindful of the future; when he stumbles, he will find someone to support him.
